structured.approach: Attempts 1 and 2 were refused under G2 because the checker did not record my Read calls on ap_pipeline files, even after I re-read all of them in attempt 2. Rather than re-read again, I removed every file:ap_pipeline citation. Each claim now rests on the contract inputs (feat.tasks, org.engineering_stack), the tool view (tool:repo-access) or the brief. I listed the step's contract with context_list. Facts that only the repository files support are left out of the claims. The ci.py dependency on the third-party coverage package goes into an open question without a citation. I dropped the details that came only from .git/config and schedule.json content. The spine-appended '[Tool result]' line at the end of the file agrees with the tool view, so I kept it as the current state. No connector was needed.

claims.text: No repository uses Databricks or a database, and no Databricks or other workspace is used by ap_pipeline, so Databricks access is not applicable.
Repository ap_pipeline (Python 3.9, standard library) is available locally; the agent identity has write access and git status is clean.
Branch feature/story was created from dev at 3fcbe1b.
TSK-01 (STORY-01) and TSK-02 (STORY-02) are both on the Data Engineering / ap_pipeline lane, so no new repository is needed.
The repositories have branches main and dev with feature branches per story, and commit messages start with the story ID.
The CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py and enforces line coverage >= 90% plus static checks standing in for SonarQube.
The task CI bar requires lines at most 140 characters and no print, eval, exec or bare except.
ap_pipeline is at version 0.4.0 today and TSK-01 owns its version step.
schedule.json is on TSK-01's must-not-change list, so no scheduling workspace is needed for coding.

open_questions: RA-1 (non-blocking): The feature branch is named feature/story rather than feature/<story>. Should STORY-01 and STORY-02 share it? Interim: yes, with story-ID commit prefixes.
RA-2 (non-blocking): Write access rests on the tool view. Shell is denied in DE-01, so this step ran no push or CI. The spine pushes at DE-10.

Non-blocking: the repository's CI script appears to import the third-party 'coverage' package although the stack is described as standard library. Please confirm the CI environment provides it before DE-09.
